newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: RESEARCH ALERT - Tenaga upgraded to 'buy'.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Tenaga upgraded to 'buy'.

text.p: Hong Kong-based Asia Equity Research Ltd said in a report on Friday it had upgraded Malaysian power utility Tenaga Nasional Bhd from a 'sell' to a 'buy'.
It said reasons for the upgrade included the appointment of new management, a possible tariff hike in August and the construction of a new plant to increase capacity.
"We have upgraded Tenaga to a 'buy' on the strong belief that a tariff hike is in the offing," said Asia Equity in its report.

Power sector analyst Amin Abdul Manap at Asia Equity/Mohaiyani said that fund managers had been switching out of the Malaysian telecommunications sector due to intense competition within it, driving margins lower.
Tenaga had been a major recipient of the migration out of the sector, he said.
Tenaga had been plagued by criticism following a nationwide power outage in August last year. The blackout resulted in a change of management, headed by chief executive officer Ahmad Tajuddin Ali.
"In addition to regaining investor's confidence, Tajuddin's main strategies are to boost sales and increase efficiency and productivity," the report said.

On the tariff hike, the research house said: "We believe Tenaga will get at least a 1.5 cent hike (up 6.9 percent), as this is still lower than the 1.67 cents (8.3 percent) hike granted in March 1996".

An increase in fuel costs and the impact of buying electricity from independent power producers (IPPs) like YTL Corp Bhd and Malakoff Bhd should give the utility sufficient grounds to apply for a tariff hike.
Tenaga is bound by various power purchase agreements to buying electricity generated by the IPPs.

"Tenaga has sufficient grounds for another hike. An increase in fuel costs and the actual IPP out-payments have not been fully reflected in the cost pass-through tariff rate formula," said Asia Equity. "Tenaga also has one of the lowest tariff rates in the region," the report added.
The research house projected net profits to increase to 994.2 million ringgit for the year to August 31, 1997, going up to 1,007 million in 1998, and 1.5 billion in 1999.
